title: Compatible presentable subobjects and epimorphism lifts for a Grothendieck weak-Serre pair
statement: Fix a universe $U$ for small sets and Hom sets [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and let $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal B$ be full replete, contain zero, and be closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between its objects and under extensions in $\mathcal B$. Suppose $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck abelian with the induced exact structure and is closed under $U$-small ambient coproducts. For an infinite regular cardinal $\lambda\in U$, call a small category $\lambda$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms has a cocone. An object is $\lambda$-presentable if its Hom functor preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; write $\mathcal C^\lambda$ for these objects in a category $\mathcal C$. Regular means that a union of fewer than $\lambda$ sets of size less than $\lambda$ has size less than $\lambda$. There is an uncountable regular $\lambda\in U$ such that: (a) $\mathcal B^\lambda$ and $\mathcal A^\lambda$ are essentially $U$-small (each has a $U$-small family of representatives up to isomorphism) and are Serre subcategories of their respective abelian categories, meaning closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions; (b) $\mathcal A^\lambda=\mathcal A\cap\mathcal B^\lambda$; (c) each object of $\mathcal C$, for $\mathcal C=\mathcal A,\mathcal B$, is the colimit of its $\lambda$-presentable subobjects, a $U$-small $\lambda$-filtered poset, and for an object of $\mathcal A$ this colimit agrees with the ambient colimit in $\mathcal B$; (d) given an epimorphism $x\twoheadrightarrow y$ in $\mathcal B$ and a map $n\to y$ with $n\in\mathcal B^\lambda$, there are $m\in\mathcal B^\lambda$, an epimorphism $m\twoheadrightarrow n$ and a map $m\to x$ forming a commutative square. If $n\to y$ is monic, $m\to x$ can be chosen monic.

source.place: Lemma A.6 (1), (2), (4), with the common-cardinal choice and intersection equality in the first two paragraphs of the proof of Theorem A.3 Hall--Neeman--Rydh, arXiv:1405.1888, Appendix A. No Stacks tag states this input; archive WANTED, online source read.

proof.text: Choose the module presentations $(R_C,F_C,G_C)$ for $C=A,B$ from the module-size lemma. Put $H=F_A(R_A)$. Choose an uncountable regular $\lambda\in U$ larger than $|R_A|$, $|R_B|$ and $|G_B(iH)|$, where $i:\mathcal A\hookrightarrow\mathcal B$ is inclusion. Such a successor cardinal exists in the universe. The counit identifies $iH$ with $F_B G_B(iH)$, so the lemma makes $iH$ $\lambda$-presentable in $\mathcal B$. Below, write $F,G,R$ for either chosen presentation.

source.place: Remark A.4, Lemma A.5; Theorem A.3, first paragraph (explicit common-cardinal bound)

proof.text: For $s\hookrightarrow F(M)$ with $|M|<\lambda$, pull back $G(s)\hookrightarrow GF(M)$ along the adjunction unit $M\to GF(M)$. The resulting module $P$ is a submodule of $M$. Applying the finite-limit-preserving $F$, and using $FG(s)\cong s$ and $F(M)\xrightarrow{F\eta_M}FGF(M)\cong F(M)$ equal to the identity by the triangle identity, gives $FP\cong s$. Thus subobjects are presentable. For a quotient $F(M)\twoheadrightarrow q$, do this for its kernel to get $P\subseteq M$; preservation of cokernels gives $q\cong F(M/P)$, hence quotient closure. Finally, a coproduct of fewer than $\lambda$ objects $F(M_j)$ is $F(\bigoplus_j M_j)$; regularity and finite support give $|\bigoplus_j M_j|<\lambda$. This includes the empty coproduct. Thus presentables are closed under these coproducts as well.

source.place: Lemma A.6, proof (1) and (3): subquotients and small coproducts

proof.text: Modules of cardinality less than $\lambda$ have a $U$-small set of isomorphism representatives: encode each on an ordinal $\alpha<\lambda$ by its addition, negation, zero and $R$-action functions. Their $F$-images represent all $\lambda$-presentables by the module-size lemma, proving essential smallness. For any $c$, the submodules $M\subseteq Gc$ of size less than $\lambda$ form a $U$-small $\lambda$-filtered poset: the sum of fewer than $\lambda$ such submodules still has size less than $\lambda$, as $|R|<\lambda$ and $\lambda$ is uncountable regular. Their union is $Gc$, since every element generates a small cyclic submodule. The union has the module colimit universal property: compatible linear maps glue on elements. Applying $F$ gives a colimit $c\cong FGc$ of the presentable subobjects $FM\subseteq c$.

source.place: Lemma A.5; Lemma A.6, proof (2); smallness made explicit

proof.text: Consider the poset $P_c$ of all $\lambda$-presentable subobjects of $c$. It is $U$-small by well-poweredness. It is $\lambda$-filtered: for fewer than $\lambda$ members, take the image of their coproduct in $c$; step 2 makes that image presentable and an upper bound, including zero for the empty family. Every compatible family of maps on $P_c$ restricts to the colimit diagram $FM$ of step 3 and so defines a unique map from $c$. It agrees on any $s\in P_c$: presentability factors $s\hookrightarrow c$ through some $FM$, and that factor is monic because its composite is monic. Compatibility with this containment gives agreement on $s$. Uniqueness follows already on the $FM$. Hence $c$ is the colimit over $P_c$, as asserted in (c).

source.place: Lemma A.6 (2), replacing the displayed family by the full poset of presentable subobjects

proof.text: For $x\twoheadrightarrow y\leftarrow n$ in either category, form $t=x\times_y n$. The pullback lemma makes $t\to n$ epic. Express $t$ by its presentable subobjects $m_j$ using step 4, and put $n_j=\operatorname{im}(m_j\to n)$. These are presentable by quotient closure. Their colimit is $n$: exactness of filtered colimits, applied to the image factorizations of the compatible maps $m_j\to n$, identifies the colimit of these images with the image of $t\to n$, which is $n$. The indexing poset is $\lambda$-filtered. Presentability of $n$ factors $\operatorname{id}_n$ through some $n_j\hookrightarrow n$. That inclusion is then split epic and monic, hence invertible; thus $m_j\twoheadrightarrow n$. Taking $m=m_j$ gives the required square. If $n\to y$ is monic, the pullback lemma makes $t\to x$ monic, and so is $m_j\to t\to x$. This proves (d), in particular for $\mathcal B$.

For a short exact sequence $0\to k\to z\to n\to0$ with $k,n$ presentable, apply step 5 to $z\twoheadrightarrow n\xleftarrow{\mathrm{id}}n$. Obtain a presentable subobject $m\subseteq z$ mapping epimorphically onto $n$. The map $k\oplus m\to z$ is epic: any map from $z$ vanishing on $k$ factors through $n$, and vanishing also on $m$ makes that factor zero by the epimorphism $m\to n$. Steps 2 and quotient closure imply that $z$ is presentable. Together with subobject and quotient closure and step 3, this proves (a) for both categories.

source.place: Lemma A.6, final paragraph: extension closure

proof.text: The inclusion $i$ preserves all $U$-small colimits. Indeed it preserves coproducts by hypothesis, and cokernels of maps in $\mathcal A$ by the induced exact structure. For a small diagram $D$, its colimit in an additive category is the cokernel of the two incidence maps' difference $\bigoplus_{a:j\to k}D(j)\to\bigoplus_jD(j)$; maps out of this cokernel are exactly compatible families of maps out of $D$. This construction is the same in $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$. Thus fullness and equality of colimits imply that any ambient $\lambda$-presentable object in $\mathcal A$ is intrinsically $\lambda$-presentable: the two Hom-colimit comparison maps are the same. This gives $\mathcal A\cap\mathcal B^\lambda\subseteq\mathcal A^\lambda$.

source.place: Theorem A.3, second paragraph: reverse intersection inclusion and ambient colimits

proof.text: Conversely, $a\in\mathcal A^\lambda$ is $F_A(M)$ for $|M|<\lambda$. The free module on the underlying set of $M$ surjects onto $M$ by sending the basis vector $[m]$ to $m$. Applying $F_A$ makes $a$ a quotient of a coproduct of fewer than $\lambda$ copies of $H$. Inclusion preserves this quotient and coproduct by step 7. Each $iH$ is ambient $\lambda$-presentable by step 1, so the coproduct and its quotient $ia$ are ambient presentable by step 2. This gives the other inclusion in (b). Step 7 also identifies the colimit of intrinsic presentable subobjects of any $a\in\mathcal A$ with its ambient colimit. This is exactly the final compatibility in (c); it makes no claim that every ambient subobject of $a$ lies in $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Lemma A.6 (3) and Theorem A.3, first two paragraphs
